key_insight: FlowMesh generates thermal-fluid fields directly on unstructured meshes, improving distributional coverage over latent diffusion while accelerating sampling relative to CFD.
engineering_relevance: Fast full-field sampling could enable large-ensemble thermal-fluid analysis and digital twins for fixed-geometry reactor cooling channels and heat exchangers.
method: Deterministic latent flow matching without grid interpolation or stochastic denoising.
L1 regularization of learned transport velocity.
evidence_signal: Across three datasets and six matched training seeds, FlowMesh achieved 91.7–97.0% macro-averaged PDF coverage, exceeding architecture-controlled latent diffusion by 11.6–45.4 percentage points, with 585–1902× wall-clock speedups over CFD.
watch_item: Results concern fixed meshes and geometries; generalization to unseen geometries or operating regimes is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Flow Mesh: A Velocity-Regularized Flow Matching Framework for Stable Distributional Modeling of Physical Fields on Unstructured Meshes
